terms.sub: Contractile and Regulatory Proteins of Muscle
clues: It is a hexameric motor protein consisting of two heavy chains and four light chains.
Its globular S1 heads possess actin-activated ATPase activity.
It forms the thick filaments of the sarcomere and pulls on thin filaments during the power stroke.

terms.sub: Contractile and Regulatory Proteins of Muscle
clues: It is absent in smooth muscle, which relies on calmodulin instead.
Binding of divalent cations to its four sites triggers a conformational shift in tropomyosin.
It is the calcium-binding subunit of the troponin complex on striated muscle thin filaments.
In skeletal muscle, it is mechanically coupled to the T-tubule dihydropyridine voltage sensor.
The muscle relaxant dantrolene blocks this channel to treat malignant hyperthermia.
It is the large calcium release channel embedded in the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane.
In cardiac muscle, its activity is inhibited by unphosphorylated phospholamban.
It hydrolyzes one ATP molecule to transport two divalent cations against a steep concentration gradient.
This sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase pump lowers cytosolic calcium to induce muscle relaxation.
It is activated by the calcium-calmodulin complex rather than by troponin.
It transfers a phosphate group onto the 20-kilodalton regulatory subunit of thick filaments.
This enzyme initiates cross-bridge cycling and contraction in smooth muscle cells.
